newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom seeks clarifications on competitor.
newsitem.headline: Telkom seeks clarifications on competitor.

text.p: Indonesian telecommunications giant PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) said on Tuesday it is seeking clarifications from the government regarding news reports of a possible competitor.

"The company is seeking clarifications regarding the matter from high ranking officials (of the Department of Tourism, Post and Telecommunications) later today," a senior Telkom official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
Reports in local newspapers named the possible competitor as Jakarta Tower consortium, whose members include President Suharto's brother-in-law, business tycoon Sudwikatmono.
The reports said it could end Telkom's monopoly in basic telecommunications services which include domestic short and long distance calls, but no firm date was mentioned.
The Telkom official said clarification was needed following sharp falls in Telkom's share prices in Jakarta.

Brokers said Telkom fell 175 rupiah to close at 3,650 rupiah on foreign selling, with a turnover of some 45 million shares, making it the most heavily traded issue on the Jakarta stock exchange on Tuesday after losing ground in London and New York on Monday.
Telkom is due to issue its 1996 financial results on Thursday.
